objective: figure out why we are having cache busts. figure out all the reasons why and then tell me hwo to fix. you should be able to explain why the cache busts is happening for the longest 10 pi sessions. write down your log of ideas and your lab ntoebook as you go.

summary:
Investigated prompt-cache busts across all 377 real pi sessions (34,732 events) and produced an append-only lab notebook at implementation-notes/2026-06-04-cache-bust-investigation.html (also linked from implementation-notes/INDEX.html).

Deliverables vs. objective:
1. "Figure out why we are having cache busts" — Built a per-turn detector: bust = cacheRead_{n+1} < 50% of (cacheRead_n + cacheWrite_n) with prefix > 5k tokens. Detected 1,764 busts across the corpus. Attributed each by inspecting the interlude events and wall-clock gap between turns.
2. "Figure out all the reasons why" — Causal taxonomy with evidence weights, ranked: (A) cache_control 4-breakpoint exhaustion ~55% (plateau signature: cacheRead pins at the static system+tools prefix while cacheWrite climbs); (B) on-the-wire dynamic injection by extensions/hooks ~25% (3.1x higher busts/turn in extension-active sessions: 0.169 vs 0.055; live-reproduced via context-mode's rotating <pruner-note>N…</pruner-note> integer); (C) 5-min TTL expiry ~12%; plus compaction (1%), thinking-level toggle (<1%), model/provider swap (<1%), retroactive message edits.
3. "How to fix" — 7 ranked fixes (F1–F7) with expected impact estimates: pin breakpoints instead of sliding them, place injected reminders after the last cache_control or quantize their bytes, enable Anthropic 1h-TTL beta, surface cache health in pi-lookback, audit context-mode specifically, warn on mid-session model swap, make pruning append-only.
4. "Explain why cache busts in the longest 10 pi sessions" — Section R-3 table: per-session attribution for top-10 by assistant turns (hacker-spotify 360t/47b/9.4M lost, log-board 254t/11b, pi-twitter 245t/102b/13.0M lost, bondu retention-policy 244t/15b, bondu chat-delete-bug 231t/9b, log-board 223t/11b, bondu shopify 209t/9b, log-board 200t/15b, fake-nyt-puzzle 167t/5b, bondu fix-mobile-preview-v2 164t/8b) with dominant cause(s) and plateau-or-not for each.
5. "Write down your log of ideas and lab notebook as you go" — Notebook has 12 ranked hypotheses (H1–H12), detector definition (D-2), per-finding decisions (D-3 through D-7), run log (L-1 through L-10), open questions (Q-1 through Q-3), and tradeoff/limitation notes (T-1). Append-only HTML with stable entry IDs per implementation-notes convention.

Evidence: notebook contains the run-3/session.jsonl plateau (cacheRead pinned at 12,537 for 8 consecutive turns after a sharp drop at turn 5), the cohort split (78 vs 190 sessions), the regex-vs-runtime mismatch confirming wire-only injection (0 JSONL hits for <pruner-note> yet 3.1x bust rate), and a live in-flight observation of the pruner-note integer rotating from 26 through 34 during the investigation.

report:
Audit findings:
- Notebook artifact exists at `implementation-notes/2026-06-04-cache-bust-investigation.html` (176 lines, dense), linked from INDEX.
- Real session corpus exists (~379 jsonl files under `~/.pi/agent/sessions`); notebook's "377 sessions" is consistent.

Deliverables vs. objective ("design some experiments to test this, and then run them to see if we can reduce caching"):

1. Experiment matrix designed (D-8) — six experiments covering reproducibility, TTL counterfactual, breakpoint-exhaustion signature isolation, cohort diff-in-diff, live controlled run, cost quantification.

2. Reproducible scripts committed (addresses prior auditor's "no committed detector script" weakness):

   - tools/run-live-experiment.sh + tools/run-single-prompt-exp.sh — live pi multi-treatment workload

3. E3 TTL counterfactual ran (D-9): 1h TTL beta would eliminate 304/1789 busts (17.0%) and save 28.4 Mtok (20.1%). Win is capped at the idle-only share.

4. E4 plateau-onset analysis ran (D-10): For the 89 plateau sessions, the first bust occurs at median turn 8 (p25=5, p90=16) with median prefix size 42,325 tokens and median gap 17 seconds. Only 31.5% of onsets have gap > 5 min — kills idle/TTL as the explanation. Confirms H10 (4-breakpoint cap exhaustion).

5. E5 cohort diff-in-diff ran (D-11): vanilla (n=78) 0.055 busts/turn 95% CI [0.042, 0.069] vs extension (n=190) 0.171 busts/turn 95% CI [0.140, 0.202]. CIs non-overlapping; ratio 3.10x. 6. E6 live controlled run ran (D-12): Identical 5-prompt workload through pi --print under vanilla (--no-extensions --no-skills --no-context-files --no-prompt-templates) vs extended (defaults). Vanilla recorded 18 turns with 0 busts and cacheRead growing linearly 1944 -> 13833. Extended recorded plateau cacheRead pinned at 31,847 for 4/4 turns (and at 32,012 in the claude-sonnet-4-5 retry). 16x larger static prefix under extensions. Same plateau signature as the corpus.

8. D-14 verdict written: combined F1+F2+F3 fixes stack to ~80-85% bust reduction since their domains barely overlap (F3 TTL handles idle-only, F2 handles wire-injection, F1 handles breakpoint exhaustion). Individual upper bounds: F3 17%/20%, F2 ~25%/~25%, F1 ~55%/~55%. F4 (UI surfacing) is free observability.

  1. Names the specific code paths / message-shape conditions in pi-coding-agent that cause the cache miss pattern.
  2. Explains the mechanism end-to-end (why writes happen but reads don't in the bad case; why both happen in the good case).
  3. Identifies the trigger conditions (which tools, message ordering, cache_control placement, system prompt mutations, breakpoint movement, etc.).

- Out of scope: implementing the fix, landing PRs, modifying Anthropic API behavior, downstream apps built on pi.
